# @vllnt/convex-suppression

> TypeScript Convex component for a do-not-contact suppression list (GDPR, CAN-SPAM): unsubscribes, bounces and complaints by contact hash, plus opt-in proof.

Install `@vllnt/convex-suppression` (unreleased builds from `main` use the
`canary` dist-tag). Peer dependency `convex@^1.45.0`; convex needs Node.js 20+
(1.45–1.48) or 22+ (1.49 and newer). Mount it with `app.use(suppression)` from
`@vllnt/convex-suppression/convex.config` and call it through
`new Suppression<TProof>(components.suppression, { proofValidator? })` from host
functions: writes need a mutation or action, reads a query, mutation or action. Methods: `suppress(ctx, contactHash, reason,
{ channel? })`, `unsuppress(ctx, contactHash, channel?)`, `isSuppressed(ctx,
contactHash, channel?)`, `recordOptIn(ctx, contactHash, { listKey?, source,
proof? })`, `getOptInProof(ctx, contactHash, listKey?)`, `isEligible(ctx,
contactHash, { channel?, listKey?, requireOptIn? })`. `reason` is
`unsubscribe`, `bounce`, `complaint`, `manual` or `global` (audit only; it never
changes the effect). The host normalizes and hashes the contact and passes an
opaque `contactHash`; the component never sees a raw email or phone, so an entry
survives erasure of the person's data. Omitting `channel` or `listKey` targets
the global entry, stored as `"*"`. A channel check also matches the global
entry; omitting `channel` checks only the global entry. `isEligible` is the send
gate: not suppressed, and, only when `requireOptIn: true` (default `false`), a
proof for the exact `listKey` (a global opt-in is not a fallback). It returns
`false` for an empty `contactHash` or `channel`; `isSuppressed` returns `null`
for an empty `contactHash` and checks only the global entry for an empty
`channel`. `suppress` and `recordOptIn` are idempotent on `(contactHash,
channel)` and `(contactHash, listKey)`: they update in place. `recordOptIn`
keeps only the latest proof (no history), removes the stored proof when called
again without `proof`, and never removes a suppression. `unsuppress` removes one
exact entry. Keys match exactly (no trimming or case folding). The only error
code is `ConvexError` `data.code` `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (with `data.field`), thrown
by `suppress` and `recordOptIn` for an empty `contactHash`, `channel`, `listKey`
or `source`. `proofValidator` is a host parser `(unknown) => TProof` (not
`v.*.parse`), run on write and on read. There is no TTL, cron, listing, export
or proof deletion, no auth (the host authorizes every call) and no React entry.
Mount it more than once (`app.use(suppression, { name })`) for separate lists.
Not a legal-compliance guarantee.

## When to use

- Use it when every email, SMS or push send must first check that the contact
  did not unsubscribe, bounce or complain.
- Use it when the do-not-contact entry must outlive erasure of the person's
  data: the component stores only a hash you compute.
- Use it when a marketing send must also find a recorded opt-in proof for the
  list.
- Do not use it when you need consent to processing per purpose, with
  withdrawal and full history: use `@vllnt/convex-consent`.
- Do not use it when you need to know who is on a subscriber list: use
  `@vllnt/convex-memberships`.
- Do not use it when you need to queue and send the email: use
  `@vllnt/convex-email`, and call `isEligible` here first.

## For coding agents

The docs are bundled in the package at
`node_modules/@vllnt/convex-suppression/` and match the installed version. Read
them, and the shipped `src/`, before writing code. The links below to `./` paths
are files inside the installed package.
